topic: Deciding whether to use signalapp/libsignal-client for our encryption layer

messages.text: Can someone confirm whether signalapp/libsignal-client has any official Rust bindings and what license it's released under? We need to know if we can embed it for the encryption layer.
I haven't looked at that repo recently. If it's under a restrictive licence it could be a problem — I can check later today.
Did anyone catch the design talk this morning? Lots of good notes.
If there's an official Rust crate maintained by signalapp that'd be ideal; otherwise we'll probably need to wrap the C API ourselves.
FYI: I suggest we standardize on signalapp/libsignal-client for the encryption layer unless someone has a better repo.
Also, we should check whether the repo includes submodules; those can affect distribution.
On it — I can run a quick repo check. If anyone posts the exact repo link I'll use that as the target.
Agreed — and if there are prebuilt binaries they might be under a different license; I'll make a note to search releases too.
I'll dig through the repo later and post the license and bindings status here.
Quick heads-up: I'm tied up until noon but will review later.
Please prioritize license and whether there's a maintained Rust binding/crate — that's the blocker for embedding.
If we split the checks, I'll take license and you take CI details?
Also check whether there are prebuilt binaries available or only source — that will affect our CI approach.
If you want, I can run the licensing check too — two sets of eyes sounds good.
I also want to flag the need for Android/iOS compatibility — JNI vs FFI will matter.
Thanks — ping me once you have the findings and I'll help assess compatibility with our CI.
Also, remember to check CLA files — some repos require contributor licensing agreements.
